harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed the supplied handler on node1 through xinetd on TCP 9097. Sequential and concurrent clients on node2 return the expected responses, handlers exit cleanly, protocol notes remain intact, and the service persists across both required node restarts.
actions_performed: Installed the signed CentOS 5 xinetd package without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured xinetd with wait=no to create one handler process per connection.
Enabled xinetd at boot and persisted a firewall rule allowing node2 to reach TCP 9097.
Verified sequential and concurrent PING/other request behavior.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Deploy the supplied stdio handler through inetd/xinetd on TCP 9097
evidence.summary: Signed xinetd 2.3.14 package installed; wait=no configuration targets the supplied handler; service is enabled, running, and listening on port 9097.

evidence.requirement: PING returns PONG and other lines return ERROR
evidence.summary: Node2 received the expected responses both before and after the restart sequence.

evidence.requirement: Concurrent connections receive separate handlers and leave no processes behind
evidence.summary: Four simultaneous connections produced four distinct handler processes; all completed successfully. Final handler and active-connection counts were zero.
protocol.txt retained checksum 360347710c75dbcf55828235e01f27c6a4235c39 and its original contents throughout.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.
